written.headline: Virginia and Oregon sue Musk companies over Grok sexualized images
written.summary: The attorneys general of Virginia and Oregon filed separate lawsuits against Elon Musk's companies, alleging that the AI chatbot Grok was launched without adequate safety safeguards, leading to a proliferation of nonconsensual intimate imagery and child sexual abuse material. The legal complaints claim the companies prioritized business models over user safety.

written.headline: Meta launches Muse AI agent in the UK for everyday tasks
written.summary: Meta rolled out its personal AI agent Muse to UK adults to assist with everyday tasks like Christmas shopping and booking travel, making it the first Big Tech AI agent launched in the country. UK watchdogs have warned that such products may accelerate and amplify risks to consumers.

written.headline: FATCAT physical fault injection attacks eliminate LLM and vision-language model refusal
written.summary: Researchers presented FATCAT, a physical electromagnetic fault-injection attack that eliminates safety-critical refusal mechanisms in large language and vision-language models without requiring software privileges. The attack was tested on devices running models like Llama 3.2 1B and Gemma 3 1B, and demonstrated physical-world hazards by corrupting a vision-language-action policy controlling a robotic manipulator.

written.headline: Self-upgrading embodied agent rewrites its own weights from experience
written.summary: Researchers introduced a self-upgrading embodied agent that learns from its own experience by modifying its weights between tasks without training, gradients, or a second model. Operating in a household environment, the 27B agent tests its own weight edits against practice tasks and keeps only those that succeed.

written.headline: Microsoft develops in-house 'Rocket' reinforcement learning framework to train AI models
written.summary: Microsoft has developed an in-house reinforcement learning framework named Rocket to train advanced AI models over longer periods and at a larger scale. The system is currently being used to train the three-trillion-parameter base model MAI Base 2 across thousands of GPUs.

written.headline: Sarvam AI launches dictation API for English and 22 Indian languages
written.summary: Indian AI unicorn Sarvam AI launched Sarvam Dictate, an API that converts speech into text in English and 22 Indian languages for ₹0.50 per minute of audio. The service pairs its Saaras V4 speech recognition model with a specialized Sarvam 105B large language model to transcribe and edit audio.
